A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOCHA. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original personalized-detection experiments, embedding simulations, ablations, computational measurements and statistical comparisons in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, proposal-based teacher evaluation, translator diagnostics, PCA analysis and relational-loss ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed fusion, PCA normalization, attention/MLP translator, dual alignment losses and frozen prototype-based personalization remain unchanged. Additional feature-extraction details clarify implementation; linear translation and sampled relations are tested alternatives, not replacements in MOCHA.

E1.justification: Both use COCO/OpenImages for pretraining or distillation and PerSeg, POD, CORe50 and iCubWorld for personalization. The new teacher comparisons use the existing end-to-end detection setting; they introduce no new dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AuXFT, ViLD, KL, KL+MSE and OFA, and adds GLIP, SKDF and DRKD objectives adapted to the common pipeline. New Table 7 also compares frozen teacher representations using detector proposals. These additions materially broaden the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Added experiments evaluate teacher features on MOCHA's candidate proposals, measure held-out feature MSE and distance correlation, and vary pair sampling and normalization. Existing training budgets, shot regimes and main metrics are retained. Expanded retrieval descriptions document the existing protocol rather than establish a revised experiment.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, Sections D.3-D.5 test linear versus nonlinear translation, quantify each modality's contribution to retained PCA components, and compare full relational supervision with Top-K/Rand-K sampling and normalization alternatives. These substantially extend the evidence explaining central design choices.

E5.justification: The existing uncertainty reporting and Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis, including Table 5's p-values, are retained. New result rows follow the existing plus/minus reporting practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: Existing matched results remain unchanged, including MOCHA's Table 2 average of 58.7. Substantial additions include three baseline rows, proposal-based teacher results, linear-translator scores of 49.3/29.4 versus 59.1/36.3 on PerSeg/POD, PCA modality contributions of 31.7%/68.3%, and Table 10's accuracy/resource measurements. These are additional comparisons, not improved reruns of the original results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(9), the loss definitions and PCA formulation are retained. The brief quadratic-cost explanation and normalization details clarify existing operations; no substantive mathematical revision, theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about multimodal region-level distillation, efficient personalization and architectural generalization. The headline gains remain +10.1 over YOLOv8n and +4.9 over AuXFT. Added comparisons and introductory framing support the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive interpretations connecting nonlinear translation to the semantic gap, PCA loadings to preservation of both modalities, and full pairwise supervision to preservation of teacher geometry. It also expands the architectural-gap explanation. The limitations concerning task specificity, training cost and prototype scaling are unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 specifies final-decoder-layer pooling, normalized visual class tokens and distance scaling, and discloses batch size 32 with iteration-time and memory measurements. It also explains controls for adapted comparison losses and proposal ranking. Hardware, training budgets and repository access remain unchanged; embedding caching was already documented in v4.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations to GLIP, SKDF and DRKD and explicitly contrasts MOCHA with AuXFT/OFA/GLIP in the introduction. This expands the positioning around relevant alternatives while retaining the original related-work structure and principal novelty argument.

P1.justification: Selected introduction, methodology and comparison passages are expanded or rewritten. Appendix subsections A.1-A.6 become sections B-G, with additional diagnostic subsections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned horizontally, Figure 6 is rearranged, and figures, tables, captions and algorithms are extensively resized or relocated. Table 2 gains rows and Tables 7 and 10 are new; dense result tables use substantially smaller print.

improvement.justification: The new translator and relational-loss controls provide more direct evidence for central design choices, while broader comparisons and clearer implementation details strengthen the existing study. These address specific validation and documentation gaps. The gains are tempered by smaller, less readable tables and an unexplained discrepancy in the new GLIP row: its reported average is 52.2, whereas its seven displayed scores average approximately 52.5.
